why: BLOCKER 2: a condition that does not hold marks the job SUCCESSFUL, so OnFailure= is never reached. EnvironmentFile= without a - already fails the unit on a missing backup.env, which is what pages; the Condition line strictly removed alerting from the case it looked like it was handling

BLOCKER 2, the half that matters most: this is the unit whose whole job is to notice silence, and it carried the same line, so losing backup.env silenced the backup AND the thing that watches the backup
BLOCKER 3: with the up-front refusal gone, a TRUSTISSUES_DATA_DIR that does not resolve is silently ignored instead of reported, which is how the empty-LIVE_ABS collapse got in
old:
[ -n "${LIVE_ABS}" ] \
    || setup "TRUSTISSUES_DATA_DIR is set to ${TRUSTISSUES_DATA_DIR}, which does not resolve to a directory"

why: BLOCKER 3 + 4: the exact original block. Resolving LIVE_ABS inline with a fallback to empty made the pattern collapse to /* and match every absolute path (the weekly false page), and the logical pwd made one directory compare unequal to itself (the symlink bypass)
new:
if [ -n "${TRUSTISSUES_DATA_DIR:-}" ]; then
  LIVE_ABS="$(cd "${TRUSTISSUES_DATA_DIR}" 2>/dev/null && pwd || echo "")"
  DRILL_ABS="$(cd "${DRILL_DIR}" && pwd)"

why: BLOCKER 4a: bash's cd sym && pwd prints the symlink, so TRUSTISSUES_BACKUP_DIR symlinked at the data dir compared unequal and backup.sh wrote snapshots beside the live database. The shipped unit sets TRUSTISSUES_BACKUP_PRUNE=1, so the next run is an automated rm in there
BLOCKER 4b: the invariant was enforced in the script that WRITES and absent from the script that DELETES. prune-backups.sh <live data dir> deleted snapshots in place
old:
if [ -n "${TRUSTISSUES_DATA_DIR:-}" ]; then
  # pwd -P on both sides: `cd sym && pwd` prints the symlink, so the logical
  # spelling of one directory compares unequal to itself.
  DATA_ABS="$(cd "${TRUSTISSUES_DATA_DIR}" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P || echo "")"
  if [ -n "${DATA_ABS}" ] && [ "${DEST_ABS}" = "${DATA_ABS}" ]; then
    echo "error: refusing to prune ${DEST_ABS}: it is the LIVE data directory (TRUSTISSUES_DATA_DIR)" >&2
    echo "       Retention must never run an automated rm inside the directory that holds" >&2
    echo "       the live vault. Point TRUSTISSUES_BACKUP_DIR at separate storage." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
fi

why: the same symlink bypass one level down: with the logical pwd the deletion site compares one directory unequal to itself and prunes the live data dir
TRUSTISSUES_DATA_DIR is set on the scheduled path and not on a hand-run one, which is the invocation the review actually proved deleted snapshots in a live data dir. The marker is what covers it
old:
if [ -f "${DEST_ABS}/trustissues.db" ]; then
  echo "error: refusing to prune ${DEST_ABS}: it holds trustissues.db, so it is a LIVE data directory" >&2
